Es compatible si rango(A) = rango(A|b);: It is consistent if rank(A) = rank(A|b); determined if that rank equals the number of unknowns and indeterminate if it is smaller. The system x + y = 2, 2x + 2y = 4 has rank 1 in both matrices and 2 unknowns, so it is consistent and indeterminate: infinitely many solutions.

Un sistema de m ecuaciones con n incógni: A system of m equations in n unknowns is written A x = b, with A the coefficient matrix and A* = [A | b] the augmented matrix. Comparing their ranks tells you how many solutions it has without solving it:
<b>rang(A) = rang(A*) = n</b>: compatibl: rank(A) = rank(A*) = n: consistent and determined, a single solution.
<b>rang(A) = rang(A*) &lt; n</b>: compat: rank(A) = rank(A*) < n: consistent and indeterminate, infinitely many solutions that depend on n − rank(A) parameters.
<b>rang(A) &lt; rang(A*)</b>: incompatib: rank(A) < rank(A*): inconsistent, no solution. When row-reducing, a row 0 = k with k ≠ 0 appears.
Un sistema homogéneo (b = 0) siempre es: A homogeneous system (b = 0) is always consistent, because x = 0 is a solution. It has more solutions if and only if rank(A) < n.
<b>Gauss</b>: se escalona la matriz ampl: Gauss: the augmented matrix is reduced to echelon form and the unknowns are solved for from the last equation upward. Gauss-Jordan: reduction continues until each pivot is 1 and the only nonzero entry in its column, and the solution is read directly. Cramer: if A is square and |A| ≠ 0, each unknown is a quotient of determinants. Inverse matrix: in the same case, x = A−1 b.
$x_i = {|A_i|}/{|A|}$, &ensp; $A_i$ = A: $x_i = {|A_i|}/{|A|}$,   $A_i$ = A with column i replaced by b
Si un coeficiente lleva una letra, como: If a coefficient contains a letter, such as k, the type of system depends on its value. In a square system |A| is computed: for the values where |A| ≠ 0 it is consistent and determined, and each value that makes |A| zero is substituted and studied separately with Rouché-Frobenius. If it is not square, look for the values where all the minors of the order of the rank vanish at once.
Con dos incógnitas cada ecuación es una: With two unknowns each equation is a line: consistent and determined means they meet at one point, indeterminate that they coincide and inconsistent that they have no common point. With three unknowns they are planes, which can meet at a point, along a line (a pencil of planes) or have no common point (parallel planes or a prism). When a system with more equations than unknowns is inconsistent, the least-squares solution is the one that makes the sum of the squares of the errors smallest: it comes from A<sup>t</sup>A x = A<sup>t</sup>b, like the regression line.
Son los métodos de siempre para sistemas: These are the classic methods for systems of 2 or 3 equations. Elimination: two equations are multiplied by suitable numbers and subtracted so that one unknown disappears. Equating: the same unknown is solved for in all the equations and the expressions are set equal. Substitution: one unknown is solved for in one equation and substituted into the others. Each step leaves a system with one fewer unknown; at the end you go back to compute the ones that were set aside.
Todo lo anterior vale igual con coeficie: Everything above holds equally with complex coefficients, as when setting up the mesh equations of an AC circuit with impedances Z = R + jX: the pivots are divided as complex numbers and the result comes out in rectangular form.
